$comment: What the UPSTREAM provider charges Relay, per deployment. Optional: with no rate card file, provider cost is not measured, and every measurement says so rather than reporting zero.

This is not a customer price and never becomes one. Oxy owns every customer-facing amount (ADR 0006); Relay measures units, reports them, and separately records what its providers will invoice it. Nothing here reaches a stream event, a usage report or an error body — see internal/providercost.

amountPerUnit is an integer in 1e-12 of the currency's major unit, the same scale as the published contract's money type so an operator reconciling an invoice against the ledger is comparing like with like. A provider quoting $2.50 per million input tokens is 2500000 here.

Every unit a deployment can report should be priced. A unit that is measured and not priced is named in the measurement rather than silently treated as free, so a reconciliation cannot look complete while being short.

A cache WRITE has no unit of its own in the contract, so an adapter that meters one folds it into input_tokens and it is priced at the input rate here. Providers charge a premium for a cache write (1.25x to 2x the base input rate), so a deployment that writes to a prompt cache costs Relay more than this card reports. See README, 'What Oxy still has to decide'.
The numbers below are invented placeholders. No provider's real rates are published in this repository.
